data.description:
## The documented guarantee is false

`docs/user-guide.md` states, as a SECURITY property of the DC backend:

> `JIRA_PAT` is read from the environment and is **not** accepted from a committed config file, so
> the credential cannot be checked into a repo by accident; the transport never logs it, and **a
> missing `JIRA_PAT` fails with an error naming the variable rather than falling back to anonymous
> access.**

The first two clauses hold. The third does not.

## Mechanism, read from the code

* `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:76` — `pat=os.environ.get("JIRA_PAT", "")`. Absent variable
  yields the EMPTY STRING. There is no validation anywhere that the PAT is non-empty.
* `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:95` — `jira_cls(server=settings.url,
  token_auth=settings.pat, options=...)`. The empty string is passed as the bearer token. The client
  constructs successfully, and requests go out with no usable credential, so Jira treats the caller as
  ANONYMOUS.

## Observed live — GitHub Actions run 30652534806, job "jira DC harness smoke"

`test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config` removes `JIRA_PAT` from the
environment (leaving it only in the config file, which must NOT be honoured) and runs the documented
`rebar reconcile --dry-run`. Expected: a failure naming `JIRA_PAT`. Actual:

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: HTTP Error 400: JiraError HTTP 400
      url: .../rest/api/2/search?jql=project+%3D+RBJUXFD+AND+...
      response text = {"errorMessages":["The value 'RBJUXFD' does not exist for the field 'project'."]}

Jira returns exactly "does not exist for the field 'project'" when the caller lacks Browse permission
— it deliberately does not distinguish absent-from-forbidden, to avoid leaking project existence. So
an anonymous request against a real project produces precisely this message.

Corroborating evidence from the SAME run: `test_the_documented_config_and_dry_run_work_against_a_real_dc_instance`
PASSED against the same harness, same fixture, same scratch-project machinery, with `JIRA_PAT` SET.
The only difference between the passing and failing case is the credential.

## Why this matters beyond tidiness

1. **The failure MISATTRIBUTES, in the most expensive possible direction.** An operator who forgets to
   export `JIRA_PAT` is told their PROJECT does not exist. They will go and check project keys,
   permissions and JQL — everything except the credential. This is the same misattribution class that
   cost this epic a debugging session on the PAT-cap bug, where the error surfaced in an untouched
   module.
2. **It is a documented SECURITY guarantee that nothing enforces.** The guide is telling operators
   that rebar fails closed on a missing credential. It fails OPEN, to anonymous.
3. **An anonymous pass can look benign.** On an instance where anonymous CAN browse the project, a
   credential-less run would not error at all — it would read a partial or empty view and report a
   converged pass. That is the "green but broken" shape this epic keeps finding.

## Approach

Validate the PAT at settings-resolution time and fail with an actionable error naming the variable —
the behaviour the guide already promises. `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings` is the single choke point
(every DC path goes through it), so one check covers CLI, library and MCP callers.

The error must name `JIRA_PAT` explicitly and say it is environment-only, because the most likely
mistake is putting it in the config file — which is exactly what the guide forbids and what this
test simulates.

**Rejected: validating in `build_client_from_settings`.** It is downstream of settings and is not the
only consumer of a settings object; the invariant belongs where the value is resolved, so it cannot be
bypassed by a caller that builds settings and uses them another way.

**Rejected: allowing an empty PAT for read-only/anonymous instances.** Anonymous access is not a
supported deployment for this backend (the guide's least-privilege section mandates a dedicated
service account), and the failure mode above shows an anonymous run is indistinguishable from a
working one on a permissive instance.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` — reject an empty/missing
  PAT with an actionable error.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — unit coverage for the new guard.

## Testing

* **unit** — `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings` with `JIRA_PAT` unset raises an error whose message
  contains `JIRA_PAT`; with it set to whitespace, likewise; with a real value, resolves normally.
* **unit** — the error is raised at RESOLUTION, before any client is constructed or any network call
  is attempted (asserted by a client factory that fails the test if invoked).
* **live** — `test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config`, already written and
  currently FAILING in the harness job, passes. That test is the regression oracle and it was authored
  before this defect was known, so it is not fitted to the fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] with `JIRA_PAT` absent, resolving DC settings fails with an error whose text contains
      `JIRA_PAT`, asserted by unit test
- [ ] a whitespace-only `JIRA_PAT` is rejected the same way, since an accidental empty export is the
      same failure with a different shape
- [ ] the failure happens BEFORE any client construction or network call, asserted
- [ ] a PAT present ONLY in the config file does not satisfy the check — the env-only contract the
      guide promises is preserved
- [ ] the live `test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config` passes in the
      `jira DC harness smoke` job, read from the JOB log
- [ ] the guide's wording and the code now agree; no doc change should be needed, so if one IS made
      it must be because the code cannot deliver the promise, and that must be stated explicitly
data.title: Missing JIRA_PAT falls back to ANONYMOUS access instead of failing with a named error
